Then do what the epic needs within the latitude contract: plan waves, dispatch one Commander per issue (each in an isolated worktree, each with a completed templates/LAUNCH_ORDER.template.md carrying pasted prior-wave verdicts, pre-rulings, honest-null clause, findings-file assignment, stop conditions, and inherited latitude), adjudicate what Commanders float (inside delegated classes as logged RULINGs, otherwise escalate), merge green reviewed PRs sequentially gated on check exit codes, and stop at wave checkpoints per the contract. At every wave boundary or material exception, write .agent-work/epic-418-followon/NEXT_WAVE.json with the exact boundary_id, launch_id, and trigger; consume exact ../constellation-replan/templates/REPLAN_INPUT.template.json and ../constellation-replan/templates/REPLAN_RESULT.template.json packets under .agent-work/epic-418-followon/transitions/<boundary-id>/; append exactly one '- TRANSITION | boundary=<boundary-id> | decision=<decision> | verified' line to ADMIRAL_LOG.md; and run python3 /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-admiral/scripts/verify_iterative_role_artifacts.py admiral-prelaunch --work-id epic-418-followon in the foreground before any next launch. A nonzero result refuses launch. The verifier requires a unique advance|repair|replan|stop exit, enforces repair safety, and writes CURRENT_TRUTH.md plus WAVE_REVIEW.md from revised_epic_body and wave_review_comment. Planning makes no direct gh/network mutation; future posting goes only through the authorized tracker port after normal gates. Log every ruling, incident, wave launch, transition exit, merge, and owned error in the ADMIRAL_LOG as it happens — an unlogged ruling didn't happen. Never run a Commander's issue yourself; never put two Commanders in one worktree. If the contract expires, a fixed-boundary proposal exceeds latitude, or the ground shifts under it, surface a contract-refresh or human decision before continuing.

closeout.title: Lessons audit, reconcile, hygiene, acceptance
closeout.imperative: The run cannot close without a record of what happened. 1) Write the epic retrospective as EPISODES: one episode per distinct thing that happened across the epic — not one per wave, and not a summary — each stating its task-intent, expected-behavior, observed-behavior, impact-cost and workaround, and each harvesting what the ADMIRAL_LOG, the crew Workflow Feedback and the Commander returns actually recorded. An episode is a record, not a rule: write what you observed, and do NOT write a rule for a future agent to follow — a rule to follow belongs in docs/agents/* and is a human's call. Write the delta to .agent-work/epic-418-followon/episode-delta.json and apply it deterministically: python3 /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-admiral/scripts/apply_episode_delta.py --delta .agent-work/epic-418-followon/episode-delta.json --store-root episodes. Pass --store-root on every invocation: the writer's default resolves relative to the installed skill directory, so an installed copy would silently build a store at ~/.claude/skills/constellation-admiral/episodes — outside the repo — while every gate reported green. Never hand-edit a file under episodes/: that writer is the only write path into it. Then run the capture gate before advancing: python3 /home/tommy/.claude/skills/constellation-admiral/scripts/verify_episode_captured.py epic-418-followon --store-root episodes --phase feedback. 2) When any part of this closeout edits a shipped compact-format JSON template, edit the raw text surgically (never round-trip it through json.load/json.dump, which reflows the file and destroys blame) and re-validate with json.load afterward. 3) Hand the epic's net change to a constellation-cartographer subagent for architecture reconcile. 4) Hygiene: every branch merged or dispositioned, worktrees swept, ADMIRAL_LOG archived under .agent-work/archive/. 5) Present the epic summary and get user acceptance. Then release the lease: <engine> release --session-id admiral-epic-418-followon.

why_trail.why: The follow-on is the last three links of #418's confirmed chain, and the contract is written to what each one actually needs rather than to a generic dial: F goes first because A2 settled the verb meanings it types and because the spec's F-before-C link is real, C's preparation overlaps wave 1 because its observables must be named before unit selection or the measure self-fulfils, and E is terminal by its own body and now reads across the redux as well as this run. The two costly-to-revert items the spec names — C's tranche boundary and E's cluster boundaries — are carved out as surfaced exceptions inside otherwise-delegated classes, and both measurement missions have their core mechanics pre-cleared per #145 so the harness classifier cannot veto the thing they were dispatched to run.

Thirteen workstreams merged. Wave 7 bound the lifecycle to the spine and the human called the stop; the w8x-closeout transition records decision=stop and the prelaunch verifier accepts it. Four of five done-conditions hold on main; the fifth is filed on #559 and #565 rather than worked.

The epic closes with its record written rather than asserted. Twenty-one episodes are in the store through the only write path, and the capture gate passes. The reconcile ran and returned a measured no-op with a receipt, because this repo has no packet map to reconcile against. The last worktree was harvested before it was swept, sixteen merged branches are gone, and the four refs that remain are dispositioned in the log with the reason they were not deleted: the harness refused the force-delete and I did not route around it. Four of five done-conditions hold; the fifth is filed on #559 and #565 with its full measurement, because the human chose to file it rather than run it.
